title: P187S mutation affects NQO1 catalysis
author: Anoz Carbonell, Ernesto
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Set up stopped‑flow instrument
steps.instruction: Install the SX.18 MV stopped‑flow spectrophotometer (Applied Photophysics Ltd.) with its photodiode array detector and verify operation under anaerobic conditions as described in reference [24].

steps.title: Prepare reaction buffer
steps.instruction: Make 20 mM HEPES‑KOH buffer, adjust to pH 7.4, and keep it anaerobic for all subsequent mixing steps.

steps.title: Prepare NQO1 holo protein
steps.instruction: Dilute each NQO1 holo variant to a final concentration of 7.5 µM in the HEPES‑KOH buffer.

steps.title: Prepare coenzyme solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the following coenzyme stocks in the same buffer:

substeps.instruction: NADH series ranging from 7.5 µM to 100 µM.

steps.title: Measure reductive half‑reaction
steps.instruction: Using the stopped‑flow device, rapidly mix 7.5 µM NQO1 holo with the chosen coenzyme (NADH at the desired concentration, NADPH, or NADD) under anaerobic conditions.

steps.title: Generate NQO1 hq and measure oxidative half‑reaction
steps.instruction: First form NQO1 hq by reacting NQO1 holo with an equimolar amount of NADH (7.5 µM). Then, in the stopped‑flow, mix the resulting 7.5 µM NQO1 hq with 7.5 µM DCPIP under anaerobic conditions.

steps.title: Collect multi‑wavelength absorption data
steps.instruction: Record absorbance spectra from 400 nm to 900 nm (flavin region) for each stopped‑flow experiment, using the photodiode array detector.

steps.title: Process raw data
steps.instruction: Import the collected spectra into ProData‑SX software (Applied Photophysics Ltd.) and perform baseline correction and averaging as described in reference [24].

steps.title: Perform spectral deconvolution
steps.instruction: Using Pro‑Kineticist, apply global analysis and numerical integration to fit the time‑dependent data to sequential irreversible models (A→B→C or A→B→C→D). Extract observed rate constants (k_obs) and spectra of intermediate and final species.

steps.title: Determine kinetic isotope effects
steps.instruction: Prepare equimolar mixtures of protein and coenzyme (7.5 µM each) with either NADH or [4R‑2H]‑NADD. Measure k_obs for each at the required temperatures, then calculate the primary kinetic isotope effect (KIE) as the ratio k_obs(NADH)/k_obs(NADD).

steps.title: Calculate activation parameters
steps.instruction: Plot ln(k_obs) versus 1/T for the temperature series and fit to the Arrhenius equation to obtain the frequency factor (A) and activation energy (E_a) as described in reference [24].
